This manhole cover just fell down its own hole.
Again. Third one today, and Gus is the guy who climbs down to get it.
His boss loves square covers. They're cheap, and they stack nice.
So one night, Gus pours a round one.
Next morning, a garbage truck slams the street, and every cover jumps.
The square ones tip on their edge, and slip right through.
Here's why. A square is wider corner to corner, so tilted just right, it fits its own hole.
A circle is the same width every way you turn it. It can never fall in.
The boss storms over to yell, steps on a square cover, and drops out of sight.
Gus just rolls the round one over.
